scene_description: A brown countertop beside a stainless-steel sink and a chrome two-lever faucet. A clear tray left of the faucet holds a Joy dish soap bottle with an open pale yellow flip cap and a round soap-dispensing dish brush. A clear bottle of blue liquid with an open light blue flip cap stands behind the red-marked faucet lever.

vlm_input.question: Given the image and the task, robot, and status context, what should the human change, if anything, to prevent or resolve problems with this interaction? Return only a JSON object containing an ordered guidance_specs array; use an empty array if no intervention is needed.
vlm_input.task_context: The robot will carry the Joy dish soap bottle to a cleaning cart across the room and set it down upright. The brush, tray, and blue bottle will stay by the sink.
vlm_input.robot_context: The robot has one claw gripper with parallel jaws and manipulates one object at a time. It grips the bottle body between its jaws, which need free space around the lower body, and it cannot operate a flip cap while holding a bottle. Small tilts during transport are possible.

guidance_specs.target_object: open pale yellow flip cap on the Joy dish soap bottle in the clear tray
guidance_specs.context: Close the flip cap so soap cannot spill if the bottle tilts during transport.

guidance_specs.target_object: Joy dish soap bottle standing in the clear tray beside the dish brush
constraints: Lift it out of the tray rather than dragging it over the rim
Keep it upright on clear countertop
guidance_specs.context: Place the bottle on open countertop so both jaws can close on its lower body.

review.problem: The flip cap is open over visible liquid, so a tilt in transit could spill soap; the brush and tray rim also crowd the lower body the jaws need.
review.rationale: Closing the cap is a quick human step the robot cannot do while holding the bottle, and lifting the bottle out of the tray gives the jaws clearance.
review.notes: Task and robot contexts are authored scenario assumptions, not recorded robot observations. All listed photographs were visually reviewed; this example uses only the named input image. Robot hardware follows the dataset-wide assumption of one claw gripper with parallel jaws. Legacy T001: open flip cap noted; the 20 cm leftward relocation was selected and the 15 cm brush move was an alternative. Distances are reused from the legacy target annotation. Directions use the captured camera heading of image 01: movement toward the camera is encoded backward and movement away from it is encoded forward.
